items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: Oh, this was during the time that I played with Duke Ellington's band. I was in the pit, and so was the band, and Duke was directing the band

ctx.x: -- Alabama, from the same school that the McCord brothers came from, and he turned out to be a great reading trumpet player. In fact, from my band he went to the great bands, like he played with Duke Ellington for quite a spell. He played with Lucky Millinder and his great band, and we called him Shad. That was his nickname, Shad or Scad -- I believe it's Scad. But anyway, he was a little humpback guy with great shoulders. When I say humpback, I mean he could play close up, you know, pumping. When you say…

I think one time you told me a little bit about how you had met Rex Stewart. Maybe I'm thinking of somebody else, but you told me the other night about somebody that came and nobody thought he could play, and then he suddenly just boomed out, maybe --

items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: they always idolized Duke's kind of liked this band... Duke had a thing going on the out chorus

ctx.x: -- (inaudible) and whatnot. And they've got a balcony upstairs, and the reason I'm going to mention this is because I had a band at that time, and they always idolized Duke's kind of liked this band. We were upstairs. And that band was playing a riff -- I don't know what it was. An arrangement, I should say. And I stood -- I had to turn around and look at my band when these guys were swinging.

We were looking down on them. And Duke had a thing going on the out chorus (inaudible) where the brass had a little corner and the saxophones had one going. When I said the brass I meant the trumpets.
